editorial_contributions.text: Summary: The algebras \(\mathbb{C}\) (complex numbers), \(\mathbb{H}\) (quaternions), and \(\mathbb{O}\) (octonions) are real division algebras obtained from the real numbers \(\mathbb{R}\) by a doubling procedure called the Cayley-Dickson Process. By doubling \(\mathbb{R}\) (dim 1), we obtain \(\mathbb{C}\) (dim 2), then \(\mathbb{C}\) produces \(\mathbb{H}\) (dim 4), and \(\mathbb{H}\) yields \(\mathbb{O}\) (dim 8). The next doubling process applied to \(\mathbb{O}\) then yields an algebra \(\mathbb{S}\) (dim 16) called the sedenions. This study deals with the subalgebra structure of the sedenion algebra \(\mathbb{S}\) and its zero divisors. In particular, it shows that \(\mathbb{S}\) has subalgebras isomorphic to \(\mathbb{R}\), \(\mathbb{C}\), \(\mathbb{H}\), \(\mathbb{O}\), and a newly identified algebra \(\widetilde\mathbb{O}\) called the quasi-octonions that contains the zero-divisors of \(\mathbb{S}\).

editorial_contributions.text:
Summary: The sedenions \(\mathbb{S}\) is a 16-dimensional real algebra that belongs to the family of real Cayley-Dickson algebras. These algebras include \(\mathbb{C}\) (complex numbers), \(\mathbb{H}\) (quaternions), and \(\mathbb{O}\) (octonions) that are the only real division algebras obtained from the real numbers \(\mathbb{R}\) by a doubling procedure called the Cayley-Dickson process.

 This study deals with the subloop structure of the sedenion loop \(\mathbf S_L\) generated by the 16 basis elements of \(\mathbb{S}\). In particular it shows that \(\mathbf S_L\) has subloops isomorphic to \(\mathbf C_2\) (the cyclic group of order 2), \(\mathbf C_4\) (the cyclic group of order 4), \(\mathbf Q\) (the quaternion group of order 8), \(\mathbf O_L\) (the octonion loop of order 16), and a newly identified loop \(\widetilde{\mathbf O}_L\) (called the quasi-octonion loop of order 16). The subloops of \(\mathbb{S}\) that are isomorphic to \(\widetilde{\mathbf O}_L\) generate subalgebras of \(\mathbb{S}\) isomorphic to an algebra \(\widetilde{\mathbf O}\) (called the quasi-octonion algebra of dimension 16) that contain zero divisors.

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: The Cayley-Dickson process gives a recursive method of constructing a nonassociative algebra of dimension \(2^n\) for all \(n = 0\), beginning with any ring of scalars. The algebras in this sequence are known to be flexible quadratic algebras; it follows that they are noncommutative Jordan algebras: they satisfy the flexible identity in degree 3 and the Jordan identity in degree 4. For the integral sedenion algebra (the double of the octonions) we determine a complete set of generators for the multilinear identities in degrees = 5. Since these identities are satisfied by all flexible quadratic algebras, it follows that a multilinear identity of degree = 5 is satisfied by all the algebras obtained from the Cayley-Dickson process if and only if it is satisfied by the sedenions.

editorial_contributions.text: In the first part of the paper the author determined the Cayley-Klein parameters for the de Sitter groups and also the four-dimensional double valued irreducible representations of these groups. These representations are analogous to the SL\((2,\mathbb C)\) double-valued irreducible representations of the proper orthochronous Lorentz group. The second part of the present paper is concerned with an extension of the investigations of quasigroups connected with the quasi-rotations in Minkowski space. The author determined the quasi-rotations nonassociative groups related to the de Sitter groups \(\text{SO}(1,4)\) and \(\text{SO}(3,2)\). Also a particular type of a quasigroup connected to the sedenion group is determined. The covariance of the Dirac equation is demonstrated with respect to the nonassociative group of quasi-rotations that is connected to the proper orthochronous Lorentz group. A similar kind of covariance is shown with respect to the nonassociative group of quasi-rotations that is related to the de Sitter groups. Also the author discusses some hidden symmetries of of the Dirac equation in terms of the nonassociative group of quasi-rotations.

Die Arbeit beantwortet eine im Jahre 1934 durch die Mathematische Gesellschaft in Amsterdam gestellte Preisfrage.

Eine quadratische, vierreihige Matrix \(A=\|a_i^k\|\) heißt -- als höhere komplexe Zahl mit 16 Komponenten aufgefaßt -- eine Sedenion. Fünf Sedenionen \(A\), \(B\), \(C\), \(\ldots\) bilden eine ``Pentade'', wenn \(A^2\), \(B^2\), \(\ldots\) gleich der Einheitsmatrix \(\pm E\) sind und wenn für die Produkte \(AB\), \(AC\), \(BC\), \(\ldots\) die Gleichungen \(AB=-BA\) usw. gelten. Nicht jede Matrix \(A\) gehört zu einer Pentade; es gibt unter den \(\infty^{16}\) Sedenionen nur \(\infty^{9}\) mit dieser Eigenschaft, und es gilt die Mannigfaltigkeit derselben zu untersuchen.

Sind die 16 Elemente \(a_i^k\) von \(A\) euklidische Koordinaten eines Punktes in einem \(E_{16}\), so bilden diejenigen Sedenionen, die zu einer Pentade gehören können, eine neundimensionale Mannigfaltigkeit \(X_9\), die durch Gleichungen 
\[
 \left\{ \begin{aligned} 4a_{\lambda}^i \, a_k^{\lambda} & = a_{\mu}^{\lambda}\, a_{\lambda}^{\mu} \cdot \delta_k^i \qquad \quad (i,\, k=1, \, 2, \, 3, \, 4),\\ a_{\lambda}^{\lambda} & =0 \end{aligned} \right. \tag{1} 
\]
 bestimmt wird. Sie besteht aus \(\infty^{8}\) Geraden durch den Ursprung, und diese Geraden sind das eineindeutige Bild der \(\infty^{8}\) Geraden im fünfdimensionalen projektiven Raum [5], also eindeutig-umkehrbar abzubilden auf die \textit{Grassmann}sche Mannigfaltigkeit \(M_8^{14}\) vierzehnter Ordnung im [15].

Zu den Gleichungen (1) gelangt man durch einen Kunstgriff: Ein \(a_i^k\) von \(X_9\) läßt sich als Produkt zweier Bivektoren, die involutorisch liegen, darstellen: 
\[
 a_i^k=\alpha^{k\lambda}\beta_{\lambda i}=-\beta^{k\lambda}\alpha_{\lambda i}. 
\]
 Hierdurch ergibt sich eine Abbildung dieser \(a_i^k\) auf die einfachen Bivektoren eines \(R_6\), und die Untersuchung der \(X_9\) wird so zurückgeführt auf die der Mannigfaltigkeit dieser Bivektoren (Ebenen) im \(R_6\).

Verf. bestimmt alle linearen erzeugenden Räume der \(X_9\). \(X_9\) selbst liegt in einem linearen \(E_{15}\) und in keinem linearen Raum von weniger als 15 Dimensionen. Die größten erzeugenden \(E_r\) auf \(X_9\) sind die \(\infty^5 \, E_5\), die den ``Pentadensystemen'' entsprechen und die durch die fünf \(a_i^k\) einer Pentade aufgespannt werden. Ferner wird die gegenseitige Lage von erzeugenden Räumen \(E_r\) der \(X_9\) ausführlich erörtert.

title.title: On generalized Tribonacci sedenions

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: This paper extends the octonion calibration in Clifford algebra to two related sedenion calibrations. Associative calibrations map quaternion rings in Clifford algebra to those in Cayley-Dickson algebras, with octonions consisting of seven rings and sedenions having 35 rings. A new non-associative calibration is found that is related to the sedenion associative calibration but is invertible, providing a classification of the ideals of the even sub-algebra of Clifford algebra. This leads to subalgebras of certain Clifford algebras and a thorough analysis of the possible automorphisms of sedenions is applied using the Spin and Pin groups. While the calibrations and automorphsms of octonions have minimal divergence, it is found sedenions introduce new algebras and this work clarifies the discrepancy in the results of Schafer and Brown on the automorphisms of sedenions. The non-associative calibrations are found to be an infinite series that matches the finite geometry PG(N,2) series, discovered by Gino Fano, but since this series can be derived from simplices the name Fano hyper-volumes is suggested. The visual representation of sedenions as the 3-D Fano volume, representing the 15 Fano planes of sedenions, allows the power-associative rings to be visually distinguished from the octonion non-associative rings. These are more than loops because the power-associative rings of sedenions contain zero divisors. The visual representation of sedenions may be important for particle physics and Clifford algebra provides analysis tools for the PG(N,2) series that uncovers the hidden structure of Cayley-Dickson algebras within an associative algebra.

title.title: The geometry of sedenion zero divisors

editorial_contributions.text:
In this paper, the author presents the Cayley-Dickson split-sedenion algebra, an algebra of dimension 16. The author studies the zero divisors of the Cayley-Dickson split-sedenion algebra and classifies them by using the dimensions of their annihilators and orthogonalizers. Based on the obtained results, the orthogonality graph and the zero divisor graph of the split-sedenions are described by using their diameters and cliques. 

The paper has four sections. First section presents some introductory notions. In Section 2 the Cayley-Dickson process and some examples and properties of obtained algebras are presented. In Section 3 and Section 4 are obtained the main results.

title.title: Relation graphs of the split-sedenion algebra

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: Viewing the Cayley-Dickson process as a graded construction provides a rigorous definition of associativity consisting of three classes and the non-associative parts dividing into four types. These simplify the Moufang loop identities and Mal'cev's identity, which identifies the non-associative Lie algebra structure. Analysing the non-associativity structure uncovers 3-cycles that distinguish between the Moufang identities and are used to identify three power-associative subalgebras of sedenions and higher level Cayley-Dickson algebras. Power-associativity introduces zero divisors into Cayley-Dickson algebras in a systematic way and it is convenient to replace the terminology hypercomplex numbers with {\it ultracomplex numbers} for the power-associative algebras. The non-associative types show that zero divisors in these algebras occur in multiples of 84 and cycles and modes are uncovered that reduce these down to factors of seven primary zero divisor pairs. It is shown that this is due to the power-associative subalgebras being embedded into ultracomplex numbers in multiples of seven. The graded notation allows the eight octonion and seven power-associative subalgebras of sedenions to be uniquely derived, up to representation. The zero divisors for split sedenion algebras are analysed and mappings between three of these are provided. These split algebras are shown to involve the same power-associative subalgebras as sedenions.

editorial_contributions.text:
Nachdem von \textit{H. Döbritzsch} (Diss. Bonn 1928; F. d. M. 52) bereits die eingliedrigen konformen Grappen des Raumes untersucht worden sind, beschäftigen sich die Verf. mit den zwei- und dreigliedrigen. Sie entwickeln die endlichen Gleichungen dieser Gruppen aus algebraisch-geometrischen Vorstellungen, ohne sich auf kanonische infinitesimale Beispiele zu beschränken (\textit{Knothe}, Diss. Leipzig 1892; F. d. M. 24, 138 (JFM 24.0138.*); \textit{Stender}, Diss. Leipzig 1899; F. d. M. 30, 561 (JFM 30.0561.*)). Nach \textit{Lie} lassen sich die eingliedrigen Untergruppen einer \(n\)-gliedrigen Gruppe als Punkte eines \((n 1)\)-dimensionalen Raumes auffassen; die Punkte dieses \(R_9\) werden nun wie bei \textit{Hoffmann} (Diss. Bonn 1928; F. d. M. 54, 719 (JFM 54.0719.*)) auf die Geradenpentakomplexe des \(R_4\) abgebildet. Der Zusammenhang ist der, daß dem Geradenpentakomplex \((\mathfrak L X) = 0\) die infinitesimale Transformation mit der Sedenion \(\mathfrak L\) entspricht (große lateinische bzw. deutsche Buchstaben \(=\) Geraden bzw. Ebenen des \(R_4\)).

Die konforme Klassifikation der eingliedrigen Gruppen ist nun gleichbedeutend mit der projektiven Klassifikation der Geradenpentakomplexe bezüglich der absoluten \(M^2_3\) des \(R_4\), d. h. aber mit der Klassifikation der im Geradenpentakomplex liegenden Isotropenkongruenz der Erzeugenden der \(M^2_3\). Ein weiteres Abbild der eingliedrigen Gruppe ist die Zyklide, die erfüllt wird von den \(\infty^2\) Punkten mit Minimalkurven als Bahnkurven.

Bei der Untersuchung der zweigliedrigen Gruppen muß man den Klammerausdruck zweier infinitesimaler Transformationen nach diesem Schema geometrisch deuten. Das geschieht bei \textit{Bohres} in \S~12. Die Aufstellung der zweigliedrigen Gruppen kommt dann auf die Klassifikation derjenigen Komplexbüschel hinaus, bei denen mit zwei Komplexen auch der Klammerkomplex dem Büschel angehört oder unbestimmt wird; es werden ferner kanonische Darstellungen und ihre Bahnflächenscharen aufgesucht. Es ergeben sich 16 Typen von zweigliedrigen Gruppen.

Nach demselben Prinzip gelangt \textit{Höfling} zu 19 Typen dreigliedriger Gruppen nebst kanonischen Beispielen. Auf die Einzelheiten der beiden Arbeiten kann hier nicht eingegangen werden. (V 5 F.)

title.title: Curvature Spinors in Locally Inertial Frame and the Relations with Sedenion

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: The paper aims to apply the complex-sedenions to explore the wave functions and field equations of non-abelian gauge fields, considering the spatial dimensions of a unit vector as the color degrees of freedom in the complex-quaternion wave functions, exploring the physical properties of the color confinement essentially. J. C. Maxwell was the first to employ the quaternions to study the electromagnetic fields. His method inspires subsequent scholars to introduce the quaternions, octonions, and sedenions to research the electromagnetic field, gravitational field, and nuclear field. The application of complex-sedenions is capable of depicting not only the field equations of classical mechanics, but also the field equations of quantum mechanics. The latter can be degenerated into the Dirac equation and Yang-Mills equation. In contrast to the complex-number wave function, the complex-quaternion wave function possesses three new degrees of freedom, that is, three color degrees of freedom. One complex-quaternion wave function is equivalent to three complex-number wave functions. It means that the three spatial dimensions of unit vector in the complex-quaternion wave function can be considered as the ``three colors''; naturally the color confinement will be effective. In other words, in the complex-quaternion space, the ``three colors'' are only the spatial dimensions, rather than any property of physical substance.
